figures.finding: The federal election to deduct a film's production costs at once (Section 181, up to $15 million of cost, $20 million in low-income or distressed areas) does not apply to productions that began after 31 December 2025, so a film starting now has no federal production incentive.

value.lastAmended: 2025-07-04 (Pub. L. 119-21, which added sound recordings but kept the end date)

figures.applies: United States, federal income tax; productions commencing after 31 December 2025 are outside it (statute as published by LII, read 2026-11-01; a later extension, if any, was not found).

sources.said: Paragraph (1) shall not apply to so much of the aggregate cost of any qualified film or television production or any qualified live theatrical production as exceeds $15,000,000. … subparagraph (A) shall be applied by substituting “$20,000,000” for “$15,000,000”. … This section shall not apply to qualified film and television productions, qualified live theatrical productions … or qualified sound recording productions commencing after December 31, 2025

figures.finding: California, the largest state program, allocates $750 million of credits a year from July 2025 to June 2030: 35% of qualified spending for studio features (up to $120 million of spending, a $42 million credit) and 35% on up to $20 million for independent films (a $7 million credit, which an independent may sell); the wages of producers, writers, directors and actors do not count.

independentFilm.definition: producer not publicly traded and not more than 30% owned by a publicly traded company

figures.applies: California (state, not federal), Film and Television Tax Credit Program 4.0, guidelines dated 1 January 2026; features of at least 75 minutes and $1 million budget with 75% of budget or shoot days in California.

sources.said: The five-year program began on July 1, 2025, and will continue through fiscal year 2029-2030. … The program allocates $750 million of tax credits each fiscal year. … 3. 35% Non-Independent Feature Films ($262.5 million) … 4. 10% Independent Films ($75 million) … The 35% tax credit applies up to a maximum of $120 million of qualified expenditures, which serves as an effective cap on the tax credit amount of $42 million, excluding uplifts. … Independent Film applicants are eligible to receive 35% of qualified expenditures, applied to a maximum of $20 million of the qualified expenditure budget. This serves as an effective cap on the tax credit amount of $7 million, excluding Uplifts. … a. Wages paid to producers, writers, directors, actors, stunt performers, music directors, music composers, music supervisors, and performers. … It is produced by a company that is not publicly traded and publicly traded companies do not own, directly or indirectly, more than 30% of the producing company.

figures.finding: The federal arts endowment's media-arts grants go to organizations (with 501(c)(3) status, or units of government or tribes) such as film centers, festivals and public broadcasters, for $10,000 to $100,000 with at least a matching non-federal share; no federal fund that finances a producer's feature was found.

value.applicants: 501(c)(3) organizations, state or local government units, federally recognized tribes

figures.applies: United States, National Endowment for the Arts Grants for Arts Projects (FY27 round, instructions published May 2026); not open to a commercial production company as such.

sources.said: The media arts sector includes community film and media arts centers, presenting organizations, independent cinemas, non-commercial distributors, public broadcast stations, and colleges and universities. … Production of all genres and forms of media art that use electronic media, film, and creative technology … Enter the applicant's legal name as it appears in the current IRS 501(c)(3) status letter or in the official document that identifies the organization as a unit of state or local government, or as a federally recognized tribal community or tribe. … Applicants must provide a minimum 1:1 non-federal cost share. … GAP Visual & Media Arts applicants may request $10,000 to $100,000.

figures.finding: The Los Angeles-Long Beach-Anaheim metro area holds most US film and video production employment: 99,061 of 158,632 payroll jobs (62%) and 5,706 of 17,366 companies in 2023, against 12,928 in the New York metro and 4,762 in Atlanta.
figures.applies: United States, County Business Patterns 2023 (Census Bureau), metro areas by CBP code (names from the CBP 2022 reference file).
